doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His first date as leader in Europe, 1954
summary: Winning a French poll, he recorded with about seven players including Sahib Shihab and Joe Benjamin, as a collective.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: It’s in Europe that you do your first record date as a leader. Is that correct?
How did that come about? Who had the foresight to know that – to recognize that you would be . . .?

I was also on the cover – I was accompanying Sarah then, accompanying – I was on the cover of the jazz magazine. I won a poll over there. That was 1954. I don’t know. I don’t remember what the name of the record company was now, but that’s the way it happened.
Who – how big a group did you have on there?
I had Shahib Shihab, Joe Benjamin. I had – I think a baritone. One of the guys from over there, and a tenor player from over there. We had – I had around seven pieces.
We all pitched in and did . . .
So a kind of a collective.
We’re all directors. Adrian Acey [?], piano. Used to play with Jackie. Because Jackie’s band was there on a tour. It was some tour.
